project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer:
One large European programme-style project that develops and demonstrates cost-effective wave and tidal energy systems able to survive harsh sea conditions.
The project combines its own research and at least three demonstrations with cascade grants (financial support to third parties, small grants the consortium passes on to other organisations through its own calls) to bring wave and tidal technologies closer to market, in line with the EU's Strategic Energy Technology (SET) Plan targets for ocean energy.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Scope and Structure

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer:
The project may work on any of eight areas, organised in three challenges; the call names no excluded activity.
Areas that can be considered:
- innovative wave energy devices, developed and demonstrated in a controlled environment
- innovative next-generation tidal energy devices, likewise
- new sustainable materials for converters, moorings and foundations
- tailored moorings and connection of electrical or other power transmission systems (cables, electrical equipment), including combined mooring and electrical connectors, shared anchors in arrays, and quick connection and disconnection without large vessels or divers
- condition monitoring and predictive maintenance instrumentation, including AI
- advanced manufacturing of devices, structures and auxiliary equipment
- installation, maintenance and decommissioning technologies
Challenges:
- Breakthrough challenge: new solutions and knowledge, by the consortium and through cascade grants
- Validation challenge: validation in laboratory and relevant environment, by the consortium and through cascade grants
- Demonstration challenge: at least three clearly different demonstrations up to TRL 7, carried out only by the core consortium
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Scope; Structure, breakdown of activities and budget allocation

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer:
Wave and tidal energy is still too costly and fragmented in Europe to reach the market and meet the SET Plan targets.
The need originates with the ocean energy sector and research community: devices must become cheaper, more reliable and durable in harsh seas, with minimal impact on health, the environment and biodiversity, and European efforts must be aligned rather than fragmented. Energy producers and consumers are named as beneficiaries.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer:
New technologies and tools, validated solutions, at least three demonstrations, a series of cascade calls, and annual progress reporting against agreed metrics.
- Breakthrough technologies, at least validated towards the end of the project
- Validated technologies, tools and solutions
- At least three demonstrations, each passing a go/no-go milestone before deployment
- Consecutive cascade calls for the breakthrough challenge (the first in year 1) and for the validation challenge (later)
- An annual deliverable and milestone reporting progress on technology metrics and SET Plan indicators
- A risk and mitigation plan, and an Advisory Board
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Structure; Governance of the project

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
Projects must contribute to all four expected outcomes: progress on SET Plan ocean energy targets, better-performing devices, aligned European efforts, and a larger, low-impact ocean energy contribution.
- Advance the SET Plan's research and innovation priorities and targets for ocean energy
- Increased performance of wave and tidal technologies: efficiency, flexibility, lower cost, reliability, sustainability, operation and maintenance, robustness and security across the whole farm lifetime
- Efficient support to ocean energy R&I through alignment and cooperation, avoiding fragmentation
- A greater contribution of ocean energy to the energy system at the lowest possible cost and with minimal impacts on health and biodiversity
Progress must be monitored against the high-level SET Plan indicators for ocean energy.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Expected Outcome; Governance of the project

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer:
The project must accelerate industry take-up and share results with the European R&D community through the Clean Energy Transition Partnership.
- Demonstrations must accelerate take-up of innovation by industry and show a financial close for each, possibly with other EU, national or regional support
- The consortium must contribute to the Knowledge Community and Impact Network of the Clean Energy Transition Partnership and share communicable results
- Progress is assessed with the stage-gate metrics of Task 12 of the IEA Ocean Energy Systems programme (an international benchmarking framework)
- Liaison with the IEA Ocean Energy Systems programme for synergies is expected where relevant
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Structure; Governance of the project

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer:
At least three independent organisations from three different countries; the call sets no maximum.
The general rule requires, as beneficiaries (organisations that sign the grant agreement and receive funding), three legal entities independent of each other: at least one established in an EU Member State and two others each in a different Member State or country associated with Horizon Europe (non-EU countries taking part in the programme, such as Norway, Switzerland or the United Kingdom). Affiliated entities (organisations legally linked to a beneficiary) and associated partners (organisations taking part without funding) do not count towards this minimum.
Only one project is expected for the whole EUR 43 million budget, so in practice the core consortium will be a broad European alliance.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · B — Eligibility, Consortium composition
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 38–39 · Call BATTERIES and ENERGY (HORIZON-CL5-2027-02), Overview of this call

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer:
The call names no mandatory partner types, but the core consortium must have proven experience in managing large projects and cascade grants.
The beneficiaries that manage the cascade calls must show sound financial management of large projects, including public procurement or calls and grants to third parties. The cascade calls must be open to any public or private entity, including SMEs, research organisations, academia, start-ups and industry. Legal entities established in China are not eligible for innovation actions.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Activities implemented through Financial Support to Third Parties; Governance of the project
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 6 · B — Restrictions on the participation of legal entities established in China

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer:
The budget is split by rules: at most 7% for management, up to EUR 24 million for demonstrations, and about EUR 9 million for cascade grants.
- Project management: not more than 7% of the EU funding
- Demonstration challenge: at most about EUR 24 million of EU funding, done only by the core consortium
- Breakthrough cascade calls: up to EUR 3 million
- Validation cascade calls: up to EUR 6 million
- Maximum per third party: EUR 800,000, as grants only
The core consortium manages the whole project, including the cascade calls and the projects they fund.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Specific conditions; Activities directly implemented by the core consortium; Activities implemented through FSTP

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer:
No type of organisation is prescribed: the beneficiaries choose one of themselves as coordinator.
The coordinator manages and coordinates the project and represents the consortium towards the granting authority (the European Commission or its agency). At submission it must confirm that it has the mandate to act for all applicants.
Given the size and the cascade-grant management, the coordinator should have proven experience in running large projects and calls for third parties; this follows from the call's expectation of the core consortium.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, Submission
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer:
Formally yes, but TenneT TSO B.V. is not an ocean energy developer, so leading this sector programme would be unusual.
Any eligible beneficiary may coordinate, and a Dutch entity is eligible. The coordinator would manage EUR 43 million, cascade calls and an Advisory Board.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 11, 36 · B — Entities eligible for funding; IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Governance of the project

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer:
Yes, as an associated partner, which takes part without funding and bears its own costs.
An associated partner does not sign the grant agreement, cannot charge costs, does not need legal validation and does not count towards the minimum of three beneficiaries from three countries. It must still register in the Participant Register before the application is submitted.
TenneT could also simply apply to one of the project's cascade calls, which are open to any public or private entity.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · B — Eligibility, Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Registration, Consortium roles and Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer:
Yes: as a core beneficiary TenneT can receive up to 70% of its eligible costs, or it could win a cascade grant of up to EUR 800,000.
This topic is an innovation action (a project that develops, pilots and demonstrates new or improved solutions close to the market), for which the maximum rate is 70% for organisations other than non-profit legal entities. The grant reimburses costs actually incurred plus a 25% flat rate for indirect costs. The call sets no Dutch national rules.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Specific conditions

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer:
TenneT could advise on, or work on, the electrical connection and power transmission of wave and tidal arrays, and on grid integration.
This is our interpretation. One scope area covers moorings and connection of electrical power transmission systems, including cables and electrical equipment, which touches TenneT's offshore connection expertise from programmes such as Hollandse Kust and the 2GW Program. Ocean energy is, however, a small and early-stage source for the Dutch grid, so TenneT's role would be marginal: for example an Advisory Board-style input or a cascade project on connection standards.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer: The project must develop genuinely new solutions in the breakthrough challenge, while the validation challenge may also take up technologies developed in earlier projects.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Structure, breakdown of activities and budget allocation

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: Mainly technology (devices, materials, moorings, connections, monitoring, manufacturing and installation methods), supported by governance of a multi-party programme.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Scope; Governance of the project

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer:
All stages from breakthrough development through validation to demonstration and preparation for deployment.
Demonstrations must pass a go/no-go milestone before entering the deployment phase.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Structure; Activities directly implemented by the core consortium

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer:
Activities are expected to reach TRL 6–7 by the end of the project and may start at any TRL; demonstrations go up to TRL 7.
TRL 6 is technology demonstrated in a relevant environment; TRL 7 is a system prototype demonstrated in an operational environment.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Specific conditions, Technology Readiness Level; Structure
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 15 · B — Technology Readiness Levels

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer:
At least three clearly different demonstrations are required, in a controlled environment such as test tanks, basins or instrumented real-sea test sites.
Controlled environment means monitored and reproducible conditions. Before each go/no-go milestone the project must show all permits for deployment, complete engineering plans compliant with standards, and a complete business and implementation plan. The proposal must show a pathway to the permits and a financial close for each demonstration. Demonstrations are selected with the stage-gate approach of IEA Ocean Energy Systems Task 12.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Scope; Activities directly implemented by the core consortium

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer:
The consortium's own work and the cascade projects must form one programme with continuous progression from breakthrough to validation to demonstration.
Cascade calls should be planned so that successful work can continue without major interruption, and later calls can support earlier winners further.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Structure; Activities implemented through FSTP

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer:
Progress must be shown with the IEA Ocean Energy Systems stage-gate metrics, with qualitative and quantitative indicators and annual reviews.
- Technology-specific indicators in each area covered
- Contribution to the high-level SET Plan ocean energy indicators
- Annual reviews set as milestones, subject to approval by the granting authority
- Benchmarking and progress monitoring, building on the framework of the Europewave pre-commercial procurement
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Governance of the project

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?
cards.answer:
The call asks for an independent Advisory Board of ocean energy experts to keep the project aligned with the SET Plan.
It must include representatives of the SET Plan working group on ocean energy, the Clean Energy Transition Partnership and the European Commission. Cascade validation projects may also cover new use cases with defined added value to end users. The call sets no co-design requirement.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Structure; Governance of the project

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer:
The call sets no cybersecurity requirement; it asks for a full risk and mitigation plan and permits for every demonstration.
- Risk: special attention to the risk that a demonstration does not reach a go decision
- Permits and standards: needed before each demonstration's go/no-go milestone
- Satellite data: if used, Copernicus and/or Galileo/EGNOS must be used
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Specific conditions; Activities directly implemented by the core consortium; Governance of the project

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
One project of around EUR 43 million is expected, which is the entire topic budget.
- Total project size: not stated
- Grant request: around EUR 43 million for the whole consortium; other amounts may be requested and selected
- Funding form: actual-cost grant with a 25% flat rate for indirect costs, of which part is passed on as cascade grants of at most EUR 800,000 per third party
Final budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 38–39 · Call BATTERIES and ENERGY (HORIZON-CL5-2027-02), Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 29 · F — Budget flexibility

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
Companies such as TenneT receive at most 70% of eligible costs; non-profit legal entities receive up to 100%.
- For-profit organisations: up to 70% of eligible costs, so at least 30% must come from their own resources
- Non-profit legal entities (for example universities and research organisations): up to 100% of eligible costs
- Co-financing conditions: the call sets no rule on cash or in-kind co-financing beyond the funding rate; the remainder is simply not reimbursed
Grants may not produce a profit: any surplus of revenue plus grant over costs is deducted from the final grant.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
The grant reimburses only eligible costs actually incurred, plus a flat 25% for indirect costs; subcontracting should stay a limited part.
- Eligible costs: personnel, subcontracting and purchase costs (equipment, travel, other goods and services), plus personnel unit costs where the beneficiary uses them
- Overheads and VAT: indirect costs are a flat rate of 25% of eligible direct costs, excluding subcontracting and financial support to third parties
- Subcontracting or equipment: subcontracting should normally be a limited part of the project and be done by third parties, not by beneficiaries; purchases must give best value for money
Budgeted costs are not paid as such: only the costs actually incurred are reimbursed.
- Caps or mandatory allocations: management at most 7% of EU funding; demonstrations at most about EUR 24 million; cascade grants up to EUR 3 million (breakthrough) and EUR 6 million (validation); at most EUR 800,000 per third party
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, Budget categories and cost eligibility rules
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Consortium roles

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Partners normally receive a large advance after signing, minus a 5–8% contribution to a shared insurance fund, then interim payments.
- Payment model: pre-financing (an advance) of normally 160% of the average EU funding per reporting period, then interim payments linked to periodic reports, and a final payment after the final report fixes the grant
- Retention or guarantee: 5% to 8% of the maximum grant is deducted from the pre-financing and paid into the mutual insurance mechanism (a fund covering sums that cannot be recovered from beneficiaries)
- Financial reporting or audit: depending on grant size and type of beneficiary, a certificate on the financial statements may be required; each beneficiary is liable only for its own debts
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 32–33 · G — Reporting & payment arrangements, Certificates, Liability regime for recoveries

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: full proposals are due by 31 March 2027, 17:00 Brussels time, through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.
- Stage 1 — Full proposal: 31 March 2027, 17:00 Brussels time; Part A online and Part B of at most 60 pages, an exception to the usual 40 because of the topic's complexity
- Opening: 3 December 2026
- Additional procedure: none; the Commission may open the call up to one month earlier or later and delay the deadline by up to two months
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 38–39 · Call BATTERIES and ENERGY (HORIZON-CL5-2027-02), Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Specific conditions, Admissibility conditions

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The call sets no duration or start date: both are fixed in the grant agreement.
- Maximum duration: not set by the call; the grant agreement states the duration in months, and extensions are possible only exceptionally
- Required start: normally after the grant agreement is signed; an earlier start is possible only exceptionally, for duly justified reasons and with the granting authority's agreement
- Expected duration: the call estimates around 5 years
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · G — Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
Indicatively, the evaluation result comes about 5 months after the deadline and the grant agreement is signed about 8 months after it.
- Funding decision: about 5 months after the deadline (indicative), around August 2027
- Grant agreement: about 8 months after the deadline (indicative)
- Conditions before starting: an invitation to grant preparation is not yet a funding commitment, since legal entity validation, financial capacity and exclusion checks follow; the partners must sign a written consortium agreement
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 30 · F — Indicative timetable for evaluation and for signature of the grant agreement
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 29 · F — No commitment to provide funding

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
The proposal must be complete, submitted electronically before the deadline, and within the page limit; incomplete applications are rejected.
- Application form: Part A (administrative data and a summary budget, filled in online) and Part B (the technical description, uploaded as a PDF) through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, using the forms inside the submission system; Part B is limited to 60 pages
- Budget: the summary budget in Part A
- Mandatory annexes: a plan for the exploitation and dissemination of results, including communication activities, and the ethics self-assessment
- Partner documents: the coordinator confirms at submission that it has the mandate to act for all applicants; every participant signs a declaration of honour before the grant is signed
- Registration: every beneficiary, affiliated entity and associated partner needs a participant identification code (PIC, a number from the EU Participant Register) before submission; validation of beneficiaries follows at grant preparation
- Parallel submission: none
- Cascade calls: the proposal must describe the objectives and expected results of each cascade call, the selection criteria and evaluation method, timelines and indicators
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility, Page limits
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · B — Entities eligible to participate
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 15 · B — Ethics
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Registration
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Specific conditions; Governance of the project

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Independent experts score three criteria out of 5; a proposal needs 3 on each and 10 in total, and Impact weighs 1.5 times in the ranking.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence (clear, ambitious objectives beyond the state of the art; sound methodology), Impact (credible pathways to the expected outcomes; dissemination and exploitation measures) and Quality and efficiency of the implementation (work plan, risks, resources, capacity of each partner)
- Thresholds: at least 3 out of 5 for each criterion and 10 out of 15 overall
- Weighting: for ranking, the Impact score counts 1.5 times
- Ranking rules: equal scores are separated first by whether a proposal covers aspects of the call not covered by higher-ranked ones, then by the Impact score, then Excellence, then gender balance among lead researchers and geographical diversity
- Budget assessment: the grant awarded may be lower than requested, and topic budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23–26 · D — Award criteria, Scores and weighting, Two-stage calls
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 28–29 · F — Evaluation procedure and ranking, Budget flexibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 31 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Cascade grants, the go/no-go gates, the Advisory Board and a 60-page limit are specific to this topic.
- Exception — page limit: 60 pages instead of 40
- Conditional — cascade grants: mandatory, as grants only, at most EUR 800,000 per third party, open to any public or private entity and with attention to EU geographical balance; the first breakthrough call in year 1
- Conditional — demonstrations: permits, engineering plans and business plan in place before each go/no-go milestone
- Conditional — Advisory Board: independent experts plus representatives of the SET Plan working group, the Clean Energy Transition Partnership and the European Commission
- Conditional — satellite data: use Copernicus and/or Galileo/EGNOS if such data are used
- Recommended: use European research infrastructures such as Marinerg-i and RISEnergy; liaise with the IEA Ocean Energy Systems programme
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-02-D3-09, Specific conditions; Structure; Governance of the project
